Source: todo.md

Known gaps and follow-up work. Each item notes how it was found, so it can be confirmed before being acted on.

Unsupported SBML constructs

Algebraic rules that are coupled or nonlinear

An algebraic rule that names one undetermined variable and is linear in it is rewritten as an assignment rule (solveLinearAlgebraicRules()), so it works in every target; that cleared all 36 algebraic-rule failures in the SBML Test Suite. What is left reaches the DAE path: deSolve, MATLAB and Julia enforce the constraint, while mrgsolve, rxode2 and ubiquity write the rule out as a comment, leave the species at a zero derivative, and warn. Open items there:

  • The DAE is only emitted when the number of algebraic rules equals the number of undetermined states (daeIsSquare()). A real bipartite matching over the variables each rule references would widen this.
  • Only species are DAE candidates (algebraicStates()); a coupled rule fixing a parameter or compartment still falls back to comments and a warning.
  • Consistent initial conditions are assumed, not checked. inst/examples/sbmlalgebraicrules.xml happens to start on the constraint manifold. A model that does not will have daspk fail at t = 0, and ode15s reject the initial state; neither error mentions the SBML model. daspk’s estini can estimate them, but it requires the algebraic equations to come last in the residual vector, which the current row order does not guarantee.
  • A solved rule divides by its coefficient, so one that vanishes at run time ((k3 + 1) * S1 = T with k3 = -1) gives NaN.

Dilution through an assignment-rule volume

Done through differentiate() (00310-00318 pass), but it falls back to a warning when the volume rule reads a species (circular), or depends through time or a state on piecewise, min, max, abs, the arc* functions or factorial.

delay

SBML’s delay csymbol passes through unchanged, so inst/examples/sbmldelay.xml generates code that runs in no target. deSolve would need lagvalue(), and the equivalent per target. Only the ubiquity writer currently warns about it; the others emit it silently.

Events

Not exported at all — they appear only as a count in the generated header comment. getEventMath() can inspect them from R. inst/examples/sbmlevent.xml has two.

Miscellaneous maths with no target spelling

The Level 3 Version 2 MathML (sec/csc/cot and hyperbolics, every arc*, quotient, rem, implies, exponentiale, avogadro, log with a base, root, and plus/times/and/or/xor with zero, one or many operands) is now rewritten by expandMathML(). What is left:

  • factorial passes through unchanged. It is a function in R and MATLAB; in C++ and Julia it is untested, and Julia’s takes only an integer.
  • root(n, x) with a degree that is not a literal is x^(1/n), so NaN for a negative x even when n turns out odd. A literal odd degree is handled.
  • quotient and rem follow libSBML’s floor definition; no suite case has a negative operand, so truncation towards zero cannot be ruled out.
  • 01282: libSBML’s expandInitialAssignments evaluates piecewise(0, 5, 1) as 1, treating the numeric condition 5 as false. That is libSBML’s evaluator, not a spelling.
  • The MATLAB ! -> ~ and != -> ~= rewrite in formulaToInfixMatlab() is reasoned-correct but unexercised: no example model contains a logical operator.
  • ubiquityUnsupported() lists factorial and delay, which ubiquity has no spelling for. Anything else it does not know falls into the generic named-call path and is reported by name rather than being in the explicit list.

Smaller target-specific gaps

  • rxode2’s ini() block rejects an infinite parameter value; no spelling avoids that.
  • ubiquity maps a -inf lower bound to .Machine$double.xmin, the smallest positive double. Harmless for simulation; wrong for estimation.
  • The rxode2 list in reservedNames() holds only what was probed: rxode2 exports no list of its reserved names.
  • A renamed compartment shows its new name in deSolve too, since compartments are top-level variables there; every other deSolve name keeps the SBML id.
  • An id that is not a valid name in the target at all, rather than a reserved one, is not renamed: 01121’s promoted local parameter _J0_k1 starts with an underscore, which R rejects.
  • warnUndefinedValues() reports “No value is defined” even for a NaN the file assigns deliberately (00950).

Found by running the SBML Test Suite

Found 2026-10-17 by converting the semantic cases of the SBML Test Suite (https://github.com/sbmlteam/sbml-test-suite, cases/semantic/) to deSolve, simulating them and comparing against each case’s results.csv within its tolerances. That run is now part of the tests: 103 passing cases ship in tests/testthat/sbml-test-suite/, and the whole suite runs when R2SBML_SBML_TEST_SUITE points at cases/semantic, and in the sbml-test-suite.yaml CI job (pinned to suite commit d6dcd2c). Both fail below sts_pass_floor in test-sbml-test-suite.R; raise it whenever a fix passes more, and ship a case or two from that fix.

1011 cases are in scope (no events, delay, rateOf, fast reactions, stoichiometryMath or SBML packages). 647 passed at 4bc2da9 and 875 after fixing piecewise/ceiling/infinity spellings, three silently wrong conversions (assignment-rule compartment volumes, rule-set stoichiometry, conversion factors) and returning assignment-rule variables as outputs, then 883 once a reaction id used in math denoted its rate and assignment rules were sorted into dependency order, then 962 after the Level 3 Version 2 maths, renaming reserved ids, chained relationals, and five more replaceReactions and harness fixes, then 1007 after solving linear algebraic rules and diluting through assignment-rule volumes. The first harness put the scope at 766 because it read an empty packagesPresent: line as a package; the counts recorded with it in earlier commits (494, 526, 581) are low for that reason, though each before/after comparison stands.

The remaining 4 failures, each its own cause:

  • 01121: an id that is not a valid R name (see “Smaller target-specific gaps”).
  • 01282: libSBML’s piecewise evaluation (see “Miscellaneous maths”).
  • 01323: a relative error of 3.5e-08 on avogadro-scaled values, just outside the case’s tolerance; not yet diagnosed.
  • 01486: object 'y' not found; not yet diagnosed.

Not action items, recorded so they are not rediscovered

  • ubiquity’s relational and logical templates have no outer parentheses (ubiquity 2.1.0, ubinc/perl/build_system.pl, the $patterns->{GE} and following entries): SIMINT_GE[a][b] expands to (a) >= (b), so 2*SIMINT_GE[x][0] means (2x) >= 0. Worth reporting upstream; r2sbml wraps every such operator in parentheses of its own (formulaToUbiquityNode()), so it does not depend on a fix. Its build_system() also needs distribution = "package" to find its own build script when called from another package’s tests.

  • libSBML 5.21.1 exists but is tagged prerelease and its only change is a fix to the Python bindings in the pip package. It touches none of the eight files patched by tools/cmake_call.sh, so upgrading is safe but pointless. Bumping the version means regenerating the bundled archive with tools/strip_libsbml_tarball.sh and re-checking every patch, since one that no longer matches fails silently.

  • R CMD check --as-cran reports 2 NOTEs, both benign: “New submission”, and a non-portable -mno-omit-leaf-frame-pointer flag that comes from Debian/Ubuntu R’s own default CFLAGS rather than from this package. The second does not appear on the CI machines.

  • A local check may add up to 4 more findings that are all environmental, not package problems. A missing inconsolata.sty (Debian/Ubuntu: texlive-fonts-extra) fails the PDF manual, which produces one WARNING, one ERROR (“PDF version of manual without index”) and a NOTE about the r2sbml-manual.tex it leaves behind; a missing tidy binary produces the HTML-manual NOTE. Install those two or ignore the four findings. The vignette checks — files in 'vignettes', unstated dependencies in vignettes, package vignettes, re-building of vignette outputs — all pass.
